The *Dvārapālavimānavatthu* (Vv 55), translated as "Doorkeeper’s Mansion," is a verse narrative in the *Vimānavatthu* collection of the Pali canon. In this text, a celestial being (*deva*) recounts the karmic deeds that led to their rebirth in a heavenly mansion, emphasizing the importance of speaking wholesome words and maintaining a clean mind.

In terms of text reuse, DharmaNexus identifies 109 matching passages across 16 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Unsurprisingly, the largest overlap is with its commentary, the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* (43 matches, covering segments §1.1–4.1) [DharmaNexus]. Significant formulaic and textual reuse also links the text to several other *Vimānavatthu* narratives, most prominently the *Guttilavimānavatthu* (Vv 33), *Paṭhamakaraṇīyavimānavatthu* (Vv 56), *Dutiyakaraṇīyavimānavatthu* (Vv 57), *Ambavimānavatthu* (Vv 79), and *Maṇithūṇavimānavatthu* (Vv 77), among others [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also detects tentative cross-linguistic alignments with the Tibetan translation of the *Saddharmasmṛtyupasthānasūtra* (D0287-2), though these represent automated machine matches rather than established parallels [DharmaNexus].
